summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from RIT with firmware development experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, FreeRTOS, and UART/I2C/SPI protocols. Builds and validates software pipelines on physical hardware using Python automation, CMake build systems, and oscilloscope-level debugging for embedded targets.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth; translated 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python, validated on target hardware with software calibration to resolve sensor jitter.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a Python GUI (PyQt + Matplotlib) for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory research environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation across a multi-engineer team.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware integration end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in bare-metal C: timer-triggered ADC scan, interrupt-driven capture, and low-level I2C driver — 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz; validated timing with oscilloscope measurements.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret — STM32 + Jetson + FreeRTOS
bullets: Implemented FreeRTOS task scheduling with mutex-protected shared memory for multi-servo PWM control; received tracking commands from NVIDIA Jetson over interrupt-driven UART.
Integrated VL53L0X ToF sensor over I2C with OLED distance visualization; validated full hardware stack on physical target with YOLOv8 inference at real-time frame rates.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo crosstalk, rolling-shutter stereo depth) across a three-layer distributed pipeline; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C multiplexer; implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ driving five servos with contact-aware grasping.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
